[[File:Naokazu Miyaji.jpg|thumb|Naokazu Miyaji]]
'''Naokazu Miyaji''' (宮地直一, January 24, 1886<ref name="kotobank1">{{Cite kotobank|宮地直一|encyclopedia=デジタル版 日本人名大辞典+Plus|accessdate=2017-01-09}}</ref> – May 16, 1949<ref name="kotobank1"/>) was a Japanese [[:en:Home Ministry (Japan)|Home Ministry]] official and a [[Shinto]] scholar. He is known as a pioneer of modern [[empirical historical Shinto studies]]. His younger brother, [https://jahis.law.nagoya-u.ac.jp/who/docs/who8-21853 Kazuchigi Miyaji], was a researcher of violets and a poet of the [[:en:Araragi school|Araragi school]].

== Early Life and Career ==
Born in [[:en:Kōchi City|Kōchi City]], {{ill|Kōchi Prefecture|en|Kōchi Prefecture|qid=Q134093|lt=Kōchi Prefecture}}, Miyaji graduated from the {{ill|University of Tokyo|en|University of Tokyo|qid=Q7842|lt=University of Tokyo}} Faculty of Letters, Department of History, in 1908<ref>[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/2950861/11 官報, July 14, 1908, Issue 7514, p.378]</ref>. He entered the [[:en:Home Ministry (Japan)|Home Ministry]] in 1909<ref name="kokugakuin">{{Cite web|和書| url = http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/frontier/projects/miyaji.html | title = 國學院大學学術フロンティア／宮地直一博士資料の研究 | publisher = {{ill|Kokugakuin University|en|Kokugakuin University|qid=Q495330|lt=Kokugakuin University}} | date =  | accessdate = 2017-01-09 }}</ref>. He held positions such as Shinto Shrine Bureau Examiner and Chief of the Examination Division, playing a significant role in Japan’s prewar shrine and Shinto administration<ref name="kokugakuin"/>.

Miyaji also taught at universities during his tenure. He served as a lecturer in Shinto history at the University of Tokyo in 1918<ref name="kokugakuin"/>, became a professor at {{ill|Kokugakuin University|en|Kokugakuin University|qid=Q495330|lt=Kokugakuin University}} in 1922<ref name="kokugakuin"/>, and was appointed head professor of the Shinto Studies Department at the University of Tokyo in 1938<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.digital.archives.go.jp/img/3231883|title=「考証官宮地直一任官ノ件」『任免裁可書・昭和十三年・任免巻二十二』|date=1938-03-11|website=|publisher=National Archives of Japan|accessdate=2023-03-07}}</ref>. He retired from the Home Ministry the same year and from the University of Tokyo in 1946<ref name="kokugakuin"/>.

After World War II, Miyaji negotiated with the [[Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|GHQ]] to ensure the continuation of shrines<ref name="kotobank1"/>. He also contributed to the establishment of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]] and served as its advisor<ref name="kotobank2">{{Cite kotobank|宮地直一(みやじなおかず)|encyclopedia=日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ)|accessdate=2017-01-09}}</ref>. His final resting place is in {{ill|Tama Cemetery|en|Tama Cemetery|qid=Q982473|lt=Tama Cemetery}}.

== Contributions ==
Miyaji was a pioneer in applying empirical historiography to Shinto studies<ref name="kokugakuin"/>. Influenced by his teacher [[Yoshiyuki Hagino]] during his time at the University of Tokyo, his work also exhibited spiritual elements<ref name="kokugakuin"/>. In 1923, he was awarded a Doctorate of Letters for his work on the historical transitions of [[Kumano shrine|Kumano Sanzan]]<ref>[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/2955372/10 官報, May 31, 1923, Issue 3249, p.798]</ref>.

As a Home Ministry official, Miyaji was responsible for shrine examinations related to shrine Rankings<ref name="kokugakuin"/>. He played a central role in the creation of the [[Meiji Jingu|Meiji Shrine]] and in the establishment of its rituals and sacred treasures<ref name="kokugakuin"/>. During his tenure, he conducted numerous investigations into traditional rites and ancient treasures for the {{ill|1929|en|1929|qid=Q18792|lt=1929}} [[Jingū Shikinen Sengū|Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Shrine<ref name="kokugakuin"/>.

In 1936, he served on the editorial committee for ''[[The Cardinal Principles of the National Polity]]'' (''Kokutai no Hongi'') as the Shinto representative<ref>「国体の本義」編纂委員決まる『大阪毎日新聞』昭和11th year 6月2日（『昭和ニュース事典第5巻 昭和10th year -昭和11th year 』本編p712 昭和ニュース事典編纂委員会 毎日コミュニケーションズ刊 1994th year ）</ref>.

== Selected Works ==
{{colbegin|2}}
*''Shinji-shi'' (神祇史), Kōten Kōkyūjo Kokugakuin Daigaku, 1910  
*''Shinji-shi Kōyō'' (神祇史綱要), Meiji Shoin, 1919  
*''Research on the History of Shinto'' (神祇史の研究), Kokin Shoin, 1924  
*''Shinto and National History'' (神祇と国史), Kokin Shoin, 1926  
*''Research on Suwa Shrine'' (諏訪神社の研究), Shinano Education Society, 1931-37  
*''Suwa History, Volume 2'' (諏訪史), Shinano Education Society, 1931  
*''Shinji-shi Taikei'' (神祇史大系), Revised Edition, Meiji Shoin, 1932  
*''Explanations of Kami Worship'' (祭神解), Tōhō Shoin, 1935  
*''Faith in Tenjin as a Cultural God'' (文神としての天神の信仰), Tokyo Publishing Association, 1936  
*''Outline of Shinto'' (神社綱要), Tōyō Tosho, 1938  
*''Shinto Thought'' (神道思潮), Riso-sha, 1943  
*''Mountains and Shrines'' (山嶽信仰と神社), Shrine Shimbun Publishing, 1949
{{colend}}

=== Editorial and Collaborative Works ===
{{colbegin|2}}
*''Engishiki'' (延喜式), co-edited with Yoshiteru Shimoda, Sebunsha, 1910  
*''Jingu and Shikinen Sengu'' (神宮と式年遷宮), co-authored with Kōtarō Sakamoto, Shikai Shobō, 1929  
*''Kōnin Seiji'' (皇任正統記), Kaizō Bunko, 1929  
*''Collected Writings on Kami Worship'' (神祇集), Taiyōkaku Shoin, 1932  
*''Commentary on Ōharai'' (大祓詞註釈大成), co-edited with Yamamoto Nobuchika and Kōno Seizō, Uchigai Shoten, 1935-38  
*''Chūnori Harai'' (中臣祓), Meiji Shoin, 1938  
*''The Divine Essence of the Nation'' (霊能真柱), edited by Atsutane Hirata, Myoseido Shoten, 1944  
{{colend}}
